```{r}
#Setting the date format for the daily mean wind data and then pulling out each year separated.
w <- w %>% 
  mutate(measurementTime2 = mdy_hm(measurementTime),
         date = date(measurementTime2),
         year = year(date))
```

```{r}
#Creating the 2022 wind speed cubed plot - what if i added wind direction or vector here?
w_calc <- w %>% 
  select(measurementTime = measurementTime2,
         ws = WindSpd_Avg, wd = WindDir_Avg) %>% 
  mutate(
    # Convert to meteorological convention (direction wind is coming FROM)
    # u = eastward component, v = northward component
    u = -ws * sin(wd * pi/180),  # Negative because wd is "from" direction
    v = -ws * cos(wd * pi/180),
    # Calculate SE component for each hourly observation
    se_component = (u - v) / sqrt(2),
    date = date(measurementTime),
    year = year(measurementTime)
  )
```

```{r}
f2 <- f %>% 
  mutate(date = date(`Measurement time`)) %>%
  filter(`Cast Direction Flag` == "d") %>% 
  # filter(is.na(`Fluorometry Chlorophyll flag`)) %>% 
  select(castpk = `Cast PK`,
         ctd_num =`CTD serial number`,
         date, m_time = `Measurement time`,
         station = Station,
         longitude = `Station Longitude`,
         latitude = `Station Latitude`,
         pres = `Pressure (dbar)`,
         f_npq =  `Fluorometry Chlorophyll (ug/L)`,
         turb = `Turbidity (FTU)`,
         s = `Salinity (PSU)`,
         temp = `Temperature (deg C)`,
         par = `PAR (umol m-2 s-1)`) %>%
  mutate(
    # Calculate absolute salinity from practical salinity
    sa = gsw_SA_from_SP(s, pres, longitude, latitude),  # Adjust lat/lon for your study area
    # Calculate conservative temperature from in-situ temperature
    ct = gsw_CT_from_t(sa, temp, pres),
    # Calculate in-situ density (kg/m³)
    density = gsw_rho(sa, ct, pres),
    # Calculate potential density anomaly (sigma-theta, kg/m³ - 1000)
    sigma_theta = gsw_sigma0(sa, ct)
  )
```

```{r}
# Assuming your data is in a dataframe called 'ctd_data'
# If loading from file, uncomment and modify:
# ctd_data <- read.csv("your_file.csv")

# Data preparation for fluorescence, temperature, salinity, and sigma_theta
ctd_processed <- ctd_data %>%
  # Convert date to Date format if it's not already
  mutate(date = as.Date(date)) %>%
  # Filter to top 30m (assuming pressure ~ depth)
  filter(pres <= 30) %>%
  # Remove NA values for all variables (now including salinity)
  drop_na(date, pres, f_npq, temp, s, sigma_theta) %>%
  # If multiple casts per day, average them
  group_by(date, pres) %>%
  summarise(
    f_npq = mean(f_npq, na.rm = TRUE),
    t = mean(temp, na.rm = TRUE),
    s = mean(s, na.rm = TRUE),  # Added salinity
    sigma_theta = mean(sigma_theta, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  # Convert date to numeric for interpolation
  mutate(date_numeric = as.numeric(date))

# Create interpolation grid
date_range <- range(ctd_processed$date_numeric)
pres_range <- c(0, 30)  # Surface to 30m

# Create regular grid for interpolation
date_grid <- seq(date_range[1], date_range[2], length.out = 200)
pres_grid <- seq(pres_range[1], pres_range[2], length.out = 100)

# Alternative approach using loess smoothing for temperature, salinity, and sigma_theta
# This is more robust for irregular oceanographic data

# Create a finer grid for smoother interpolation
date_grid <- seq(date_range[1], date_range[2], length.out = 300)
pres_grid <- seq(pres_range[1], pres_range[2], length.out = 150)

# Function to interpolate using loess (more robust for oceanographic data)
loess_interp <- function(data, x_var, y_var, z_var, x_grid, y_grid, span = 0.01) {
  # Create prediction grid
  pred_grid <- expand.grid(x = x_grid, y = y_grid)
  names(pred_grid) <- c(x_var, y_var)
  
  # Fit loess model
  formula_str <- paste(z_var, "~", x_var, "+", y_var)
  loess_model <- loess(as.formula(formula_str), data = data, span = span, degree = 1)
  
  # Predict on grid
  pred_values <- predict(loess_model, newdata = pred_grid)
  
  # Return as matrix
  matrix(pred_values, nrow = length(x_grid), ncol = length(y_grid))
}

# Perform interpolation for fluorescence using original method
interp_fluor <- with(ctd_processed, 
                     interp(x = date_numeric, y = pres, z = f_npq,
                           xo = date_grid, yo = pres_grid,
                           linear = TRUE, extrap = FALSE))

# Use loess for temperature (more robust)
temp_matrix <- loess_interp(ctd_processed, "date_numeric", "pres", "t", 
                           date_grid, pres_grid, span = 0.01)

# Use loess for salinity (more robust) - NEW
salinity_matrix <- loess_interp(ctd_processed, "date_numeric", "pres", "s", 
                               date_grid, pres_grid, span = 0.01)

# Use loess for sigma_theta (more robust)
sigma_theta_matrix <- loess_interp(ctd_processed, "date_numeric", "pres", "sigma_theta", 
                                  date_grid, pres_grid, span = 0.01)

# Convert interpolated data to long format for ggplot
interp_df <- expand.grid(date_numeric = date_grid,
                        pres = pres_grid) %>%
  mutate(
    f_npq = as.vector(interp_fluor$z),
    temperature = as.vector(temp_matrix),
    salinity = as.vector(salinity_matrix),  # Added salinity
    sigma_theta = as.vector(sigma_theta_matrix),
    date = as.Date(date_numeric, origin = "1970-01-01")
  )

# Create a more conservative data mask based on actual data coverage
create_conservative_mask <- function(interp_df, ctd_processed) {
  interp_df$valid_temp <- TRUE
  interp_df$valid_salinity <- TRUE  # Added salinity validity
  interp_df$valid_sigma <- TRUE
  
  # Get data boundaries for each date
  data_summary <- ctd_processed %>%
    group_by(date_numeric) %>%
    summarise(
      min_pres = min(pres, na.rm = TRUE),
      max_pres = max(pres, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = 'drop'
    )
  
  # Find date range with data
  date_range_data <- range(ctd_processed$date_numeric)
  
  for(i in 1:nrow(interp_df)) {
    current_date <- interp_df$date_numeric[i]
    current_pres <- interp_df$pres[i]
    
    # Check if date is within data coverage
    if(current_date < date_range_data[1] || current_date > date_range_data[2]) {
      interp_df$valid_temp[i] <- FALSE
      interp_df$valid_salinity[i] <- FALSE  # Added salinity validity
      interp_df$valid_sigma[i] <- FALSE
      next
    }
    
    # Find nearest date in data
    date_diff <- abs(data_summary$date_numeric - current_date)
    nearest_idx <- which.min(date_diff)
    
    # Only keep if within reasonable depth range and not too far from data temporally
    if(date_diff[nearest_idx] > 1.5 || # More than 1.5 days from data
       current_pres > data_summary$max_pres[nearest_idx] + 2 || # Below data range
       current_pres < data_summary$min_pres[nearest_idx] - 1) {  # Above data range
      interp_df$valid_temp[i] <- FALSE
      interp_df$valid_salinity[i] <- FALSE  # Added salinity validity
      interp_df$valid_sigma[i] <- FALSE
    }
  }
  
  return(interp_df)
}

# Apply conservative mask
interp_df <- create_conservative_mask(interp_df, ctd_processed)
interp_df$temperature[!interp_df$valid_temp] <- NA
interp_df$sigma_theta[!interp_df$valid_sigma] <- NA

fluor_palette_v3 <- colorRampPalette(c(
  "#08306b",  # Deep navy blue
  "#1f4e7a",  # Dark blue
  "#2e6b89",  # Medium blue
  "#4d8fc7",  # Bright blue
  "#2fb3d4",  # Vivid cyan-blue (bloom threshold)
  "#00a693",  # Bright teal
  "#4daf4a",  # Vibrant green
  "#8cc152",  # Lime green
  "#ffd23f",  # Bright yellow
  "#ff8c42",  # Vivid orange
  "#e74c3c"   # Bold red-orange
))

colors_v3 <- fluor_palette_v3(50)

# Function to create breaks that emphasize bloom threshold
create_fluor_breaks <- function(max_val = 50, bloom_threshold = 5) {
  # More breaks in the 0-10 range to capture bloom dynamics
  c(0, 1, 2, 3, 4, bloom_threshold, 7, 10, 15, 20, 30, 40, max_val)
}

interp_df <- mutate(interp_df, date = as.POSIXct(date))
```

```{r}
# Create the section plot with temperature isotherms
interp_14 <- ggplot(interp_df, aes(x = date, y = pres)) +
  # Fluorescence background
  geom_raster(aes(fill = f_npq)) +
  
  # Color scale for fluorescence
  scale_fill_gradientn(colors = colors_v3,
                       values = scales::rescale(c(0, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50)),
                       name = "Fl",
                       guide = guide_colorbar(
                         title.position = "top",
                         title.hjust = 0.5,
                         barwidth = 1,
                         barheight = 8,
                         frame.colour = "black",
                         frame.linewidth = 0.5
                       )) +
  
  # Add 10°C isotherm contour (cool blue for cooler water)
  geom_contour(aes(z = temperature), 
               breaks = 10, 
               color = "#2166ac", 
               linewidth = 1.5, 
               alpha = 0.8,
               linetype = "solid") +
  
  # Add 12.5°C isotherm contour (warm coral for warmer water)
  geom_contour(aes(z = temperature), 
               breaks = 12.5, 
               color = "#d73027", 
               linewidth = 1.5, 
               alpha = 0.8,
               linetype = "solid") +
  
    geom_contour(aes(z = sigma_theta), 
               breaks = 24, 
               color = "#5e3c99", 
               linewidth = 1.5, 
               alpha = 0.8,
               linetype = "solid") +
  
    geom_contour(aes(z = salinity), 
               breaks = 30, 
               color = "black", 
               linewidth = 1.5, 
               alpha = 0.8,
               linetype = "solid") +
  
  # Add contour labels for 10°C line
  geom_text_contour(aes(z = temperature, label = paste0(after_stat(level), "°C")), 
                    breaks = 10, 
                    color = "#2166ac", 
                    size = 3.8,
                    fontface = "bold",
                    stroke = 0.3,
                    stroke.color = "white",
                    label.padding = unit(0.15, "lines")) +
  
  # Add contour labels for 12.5°C line
  geom_text_contour(aes(z = temperature, label = paste0(after_stat(level), "°C")), 
                  breaks = 12.5, 
                  color = "#d73027", 
                  size = 3.8,
                  fontface = "bold",
                  stroke = 0.3,
                  stroke.color = "white",
                  label.padding = unit(0.15, "lines")) +
  
geom_text_contour(aes(z = sigma_theta, label = paste0(after_stat(level), " σθ")),

                    size = 3.8,
                    fontface = "bold",
                    stroke = 0.3,
                    stroke.color = "white",
                    label.padding = unit(0.15, "lines")) +
  
  geom_text_contour(aes(z = salinity, label = paste0(after_stat(level), " PSU")),
                    breaks = 30, 
                    color = "black", 
                    size = 3.8,
                    fontface = "bold",
                    stroke = 0.3,
                    stroke.color = "white",
                    label.padding = unit(0.15, "lines")) +
  
  # Flip y-axis so surface is at top
  scale_y_reverse(name = "Pressure (dbar)", expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_x_datetime(limits = as_datetime(c("2013-04-01 00:00:00",
                                          "2013-10-01 00:00:00")),
                   expand = c(0, 0),
                   date_breaks = "15 days",
                   date_labels = "%m-%d") +
  
  # Add original data points
  # geom_point(data = ctd_processed,
  #            aes(x = as.Date(date_numeric, origin = "1970-01-01"),
  #                y = pres, fill = f_npq),
  #            size = 0.1, alpha = 0.7, shape = 21, color = "black") +
  
  # Theming
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    text = element_text(size = 24, color = "black"),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 24, face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "right",
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    axis.title.x = element_blank()
  )
```

```{r}
density_diff <- f2 %>%
  # Filter to only the depths we're interested in
  filter(pres %in% c(2, 30)) %>%
  # Remove any rows with missing density values
  filter(!is.na(density)) %>%
  # Group by cast_pk to calculate differences within each cast
  group_by(castpk) %>%
  # Check that we have both depths for each cast
  filter(n() == 2, all(c(2, 30) %in% pres)) %>%
  # Calculate the density difference (30m - 2m)
  summarise(
    # Retain date and station (taking the first value since they should be the same within a cast)
    date = first(date),
    station = first(station),
    # Calculate density difference
    density_diff = density[pres == 30] - density[pres == 2],
    # Optional: also keep the individual density values for reference
    density_2m = density[pres == 2],
    density_30m = density[pres == 30],
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  # Arrange by date for easier viewing
  arrange(date)
```
